A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain 30 readable pages, including Appendices A–R. Text comparison and visual inspection support reliable comparison of the equations, figures, tables, and appendices.

before.justification: v2 reports original MARL simulation results in Section 5 and the appendices, including matrix games, Multi-goal-capture, tag, football, and HetGPS experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and their numerical results, learning curves, and policy visualizations in Section 5 and the appendices.

M1.justification: HetGPS, its gradient-based environment updates, policy-training loops, and alternating/concurrent schedules remain identical in Section 4, Algorithm 1, and Appendix P.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same continuous and discrete matrix games, Multi-goal-capture, 2v2 tag, and VMAS football scenarios. Appendix coverage, including observability and adverse-initialization experiments, is unchanged.

E2.justification: The same shared-parameter homogeneous and independent-parameter heterogeneous policies participate in the corresponding comparisons. No evaluated comparator is added, removed, or revised.

E3.justification: Training budgets, agent/task counts, reward configurations, sensing ranges, and testing procedures are unchanged. Both retain 12M frames for the N=M=4 matrix games, 30M for capture/tag, and 90M for the main HetGPS experiments.

E4.justification: Both retain the scalability analysis in Appendix J.4, behavioral case studies in Appendices K–M, observability analysis in Appendix N, and adverse-initialization robustness experiment in Appendix Q.

E5.justification: Mean-and-standard-deviation reporting and seed counts remain unchanged, including nine seeds for the main matrix-game and capture/tag results, thirteen for the main HetGPS experiments, and three for Table 11.

E6.justification: Numerical results, plotted curves, and qualitative findings match throughout. For example, both report the football gain 1.76±0.72 for U=min, T=max in Table 10 and identical adverse-initialization results in Table 11. Figure 4b changes only legend styling.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Theorems 3.1–3.4, and their proofs are unchanged. The additional derivations and formalizations in Appendices E–I, O, and P are also retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same claims about reward curvature, the benefits of behavioral heterogeneity, and HetGPS discovering favorable reward regimes.

C2.justification: Interpretations of negative empirical gains, neural versus behavioral heterogeneity, and observability remain unchanged. Appendices P and R retain the same convergence qualifications, differentiability requirements, and theoretical scope limitations.

D1.justification: Appendices A–C retain identical compute estimates, hardware, network architecture, software, and code/configuration access information. The added funding acknowledgement introduces no technical or reproducibility changes.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. The Garey reference moves from page 10 to page 11 because of the new acknowledgement; it is not a citation addition.

P1.justification: v3 adds an acknowledgements and funding-disclosure section on page 10 naming ERC and ARL support, removes the conference header, and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. The scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 removes the running header and rule, locally reflows the references around the acknowledgement, and darkens several Figure 4b legend labels. Figures, tables, captions, and plotted results otherwise retain their presentation.

improvement.justification: The funding acknowledgement and darker Figure 4b labels provide small transparency and readability benefits. However, the scientific argument, evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations remain unchanged throughout both PDFs and their appendices, leaving no meaningful overall quality difference.
